card.name: The word most before often/consistently
card.fires_on: The word "most" used as an adverb after a reported adverse effect, just before "consistently", "often", "frequently" or "likely". It appears in warnings about where or in whom an effect occurs.

modes.label: Most + consistently
modes.description: "most" after "has been observed" in a thrombotic risk warning.
modes.example: The increase in CV thrombotic risk has been observed<< most>> consistently at higher doses.

modes.label: Most + often/frequently
modes.description: "most" after a comma, following a reported adverse event, before often or frequently.
modes.example: ACE inhibitors have been associated with agranulocytosis and bone marrow depression,<< most>> frequently in patients with renal impairment

card.plain: It marks the word "most" when it introduces how often or in whom a side effect shows up.
evidence: The increase in CV thrombotic risk has been observed<< most>> consistently at higher doses.
Kaposi’s sarcoma has been reported to occur in patients receiving corticosteroid therapy,<< most>> often for chronic conditions.
This is<< most>> likely to occur within the first few weeks
